text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigeria's Petroluem Trust Fund, set up to provide improved social services nationwide with profits from a 1994 fuel price hike, is to assist in rebuilding the country's rail tracks, head of the agency Muhammadu Buhari says. The Chinese already have a contract to rehabilitate the ailing railway system.

- Government appoints an 18-man committe to manage affairs of the local unit of U.S. oil firm Ashland Inc. Its operating licence was revoked in June when authorities said the company was trying to transfer it to a third party.
- Niece of military ruler General Sani Abacha dies in northeastern town of Maiduguri six hours before her wedding. The cause of death was not disclosed.
- Umaru Dikko, ex-Nigerian minister and close ally of Abacha, says he will contest next year's presidential elections whether or not the military ruler enters the race.
